diagnostic_evidence.quote: Finally, we stress that the assumption $C_\rho \approx 1$ is essential:

issues.failure_explanation: C_rho is a supremum over infinitely many wavevectors. For generic (e.g. uniformly random) positions, Kronecker's theorem gives k with all phases close to sign(rho_j). Then C_rho is about (sum|rho_j|)^2/||rho||^2, which is of order n (about 2n/pi for Gaussian charges). Cancellation holds only on average (E|rho^(k)|^2=||rho||^2), not in the max.

failure_location.quote: In such cases, it is reasonable to assume that $C_\rho \approx 1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the uniform max by an expectation over random positions (E|rho^(k)|^2=||rho||^2 for k≠0). The bounds then become expected-error bounds with C_rho replaced by 1.
issues.overall_effect: The C_rho≈1 substitution underlying the closed-form models and the parameter selection is not justified by the rigorous bounds. Those bounds deliver about a sqrt(n) larger error.
issues.title: C_rho≈1 is incompatible with C_rho defined as a max over all of Z^3
issues.why_classification: Needs a contained probabilistic restatement; the resulting estimates remain comparable.

This comes from bounding the in-band integral over [omega_*,omega_max] by the whole band [0,omega_max]. Hence C_*(2pi/lambda_0^2 - c_s) is about c_s(omega_max/omega_*)^2.
